editorial:
You follow Nicholas Hathaway, a hacker pulled from prison to help track a dangerous cybercrime ring. He teams up with American and Chinese agents, and the chase moves from Chicago to Los Angeles, Hong Kong, and Jakarta. The movie feels like a globe-trotting thriller with a tech twist, mixing street-level danger with computer crime. Chris Hemsworth plays Hathaway with a rough, physical edge, so the story never feels like people just typing at screens. You get shootouts, chases, and tense moments as the team gets closer to the people behind the attacks. The nuclear plant incident raises the stakes and makes the threat feel bigger than a normal hacking case.

The action is sharp and the locations look great, especially in Hong Kong and Jakarta. The pacing can feel uneven, and some tech talk may be hard to follow, but the movie keeps moving. If you like crime thrillers with real-world stakes, this is a solid pick. Watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Hathaway tracks the cybercriminal to Jakarta and confronts him after a violent showdown. The villain is killed, and Hathaway escapes with his partner. The attack on the nuclear plant was only the start of a bigger plan to manipulate stock markets and cause chaos. Hathaway chooses freedom over going back to prison, walking away with his partner as the case closes. You are left with a tense, personal ending rather than a neat wrap-up.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crime thrillers with tech danger and globe-trotting action.
